author: The King who cannot move
text_post: Not my best work by far. Just an idea I've been toying with to highlight the absurdity of the whole "4 in 5 college women will be raped" nonsense. So instead of creating a culture of fear over rape, I've made it assault and robbery, and instead of men being stereotyped, I've stereotyped African-Americans. I also included the little statistical snippet which reflects the academic fraud the "campus rape advocates" so frequently like to cite, the bit about how some women were counted as having been raped even though they themselves did not consider it to be so.  I didn't really want the Pulp Fiction meme, but it is too early in the day for me to go mucking about looking for a more appropriate photo.

text_post: Samuel L Jackson is just about the least sympathetic figure for combating sjw. Whatever you attach his image to is going to have an innate 'race baiter' feel. I dunno if you saw him pull the race card in that interview, but he thinks its funny to misappropriate the 'race card' and abuse innocents with it. He doesn't have a real respect for racial equality. Nobody who did would use it is such a profane manner. It would be like if your granny was murdered by the nazis, and you wanted to jerk some guys chain by falsely accusing him of being a granny-murdering nazi. You simply wouldn't use that trope to jerk someone's chain. On a personal level, I can't stand his professional persona. I don't like loud ppl to begin with, but especially ones who are angry, underinformed, devoid of curiosity, and unapologetic. The characters he plays are just annoying. His recent endorsement of corporate banksters is funny tho. There he is practically yelling about the pretended virtues of capital one, who want to rape your wallet.
